The August 1, 2018 FOMC statement is clearly upbeat on growth and labor, with inflation near the symmetric 2% objective and risks described as roughly balanced. Incorporating the April 2018 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) tempers this positivity: banks reported wider loan rate spreads (a mild price-term tightening), changes to credit policies in commercial real estate, and shifting CRE loan demand, while standards for qualified-mortgage jumbo residential loans were largely unchanged. These SLOOS signals of selective tightening—especially in CRE—alongside steady mortgage standards are consistent with the Committee’s cautious, gradual normalization and balanced-risk language. Netting the strong macro backdrop with modest tightening in bank lending terms, the overall tone remains moderately positive but slightly restrained.
